Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Health Systems Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing your questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Health Systems' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are Mike Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; David Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lisa Patel, Chief Medical Officer; Karen Lopez, Chief Operating Officer; Tom Ellis, Chief Strategy Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Information Officer; Emily Grant, Chief Human Resources Officer; and Mark Reynolds, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mike Rivera.

Mike Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on the impact of seasonality and external factors like the flu season, the impact of our cost reduction initiatives, initiatives to improve our operating margin, the impact of value-based care contracts on reimbursement, our operating margin performance year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, trends in inpatient versus outpatient volumes, the percentage of revenue from Medicare, Medicaid, commercial insurance, and self-pay, and same-facility volume and revenue growth guidance for the next quarter and full year.

These areas highlight our resilience and strategic positioning across our 50-hospital footprint in 18 states. I'll touch on them at a high level now, and David will provide deeper financial insights shortly. Now, I’ll turn the call over to David Chen to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

David Chen:
Thank you, Mike. Good morning, everyone. As Mike mentioned, we had an exceptionally strong quarter. Net revenue for the third quarter was $4.9 billion, an increase of 9.2% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix, the successful implementation of our revenue cycle management initiatives, and the impact of our strategic acquisitions.

Our operating expenses were $4.25 billion, representing 86.7% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in supply chain and labor optimization.

Net income for the quarter was $385 million, or $1.52 per share. We are pleased with our financial performance and are raising our guidance for the full year.

To build on Mike's overview, let me dive deeper into those eight key aspects, starting with the impact of seasonality and external factors, particularly the respiratory virus season that influenced our results.

In our sector, these patterns are annual occurrences but can intensify with broader economic and health trends. Our proactive modeling helped us navigate them effectively across our network. The 2023-2024 flu season, led by Influenza A H3N2 strains according to CDC data, peaked from late September through November, right in line with our Q3. This led to a 14% year-over-year rise in adjusted patient days to 1.82 million, surpassing our typical Q3 average of 8-10%. ED volumes jumped 17% to 2.25 million visits, with flu cases making up 21% of them, compared to 13% last year. This translated to inpatient admissions, lifting our average daily census by 12% to 27,800 occupied beds.

On revenue, seasonality added about $275 million, or 7% of our $4.9 billion net patient service revenue. Acute inpatient revenue rose 15% year-over-year, supported by a 2-point increase in case mix index to 1.84 from higher-acuity cases needing ventilation and longer stays. Average length of stay edged up to 4.6 days from 4.4, while observation stays grew 23%. Outpatient services, like our ASCs, saw a steadier 7.5% increase, as flu patients often delayed electives.

Payer dynamics enhanced this: Medicare FFS admissions, our top reimbursers at around $14,000 per case under IPPS, increased 18%, aided by CMS's 2.9% FY2025 update. Commercial volumes rose 12%, though rates were tighter from talks with major Blues payers, which are 31% of revenue.

Regionally, Northeast areas like New York and Massachusetts, 24% of beds, saw 20% higher flu admissions due to weather and vaccination rates around 49% for seniors, pushing ICU to 90% peaks but lifting EBITDA margins to 27%, up 400 basis points. Sunbelt spots in Florida and Texas, 42% of capacity, had a 9% volume bump, helped by warmer weather and our vaccination drives with CVS, hitting 61% uptake. This variance prompted $42 million in CapEx for Northeast surge beds, including expansions at key sites.

Other factors included a minor COVID uptick, adding 7% to admissions at 43,000, with CMS 20% add-ons bringing $58 million. Costs rose for PPE and drugs like Paxlovid, up 10% to $205 million, and agency RNs at 14% peaks, raising cost per adjusted discharge to $11,700, up 4%. Yet EBITDA margin stayed at 22.3%, thanks to tight controls.

We've countered with our ApexFlow analytics, integrated with Epic and ML on historical data, predicting volumes at 91% accuracy, pre-staffing 1,100 flex nurses and cutting agency by 17%. Virtual triage handled 32% of mild cases, diverting 115,000 ED visits, similar to HCA's approach. Our 440 clinics gave 1.15 million flu shots, up 19%, via Seqirus partnerships.

Ahead, Q4 expects 9-11% volume from flu tail, offset by RSV vaccines like Arexvy and site-neutral reforms. Guidance includes $140-190 million uplift, EBITDA 21-23%. Long-term, we're eyeing divestitures in volatile Northeast for Sunbelt M&A.

Next, the impact of our cost reduction initiatives, which generated over $180 million in annualized run-rate savings, beating our $145 million goal by 24%, fueling a 200 basis point EBITDA margin gain to 18.6%.

Pillars include labor at 44% of savings ($79 million): With labor at 53% of costs amid 16% RN vacancies per NSI data, AI tools like ShiftMed cut agency use 40% to 6.5% of hours, overtime down 24% via scheduling on CMI and flu trends. LOS improved 4% to 4.2 days on sepsis and CHF paths. Texas (17 hospitals) led with 5.8% LOS drop for $42 million savings; Midwest trailed at 2.5%.

Sunbelt (TX, FL, AZ: 66% beds) saw labor per discharge fall 8.2% to $4,100 vs. peers' $4,420. Midwest union issues limited to 4.8%, but wage ties to retention help. Payer mix steady at 47% Medicare, 33% commercial, 14% Medicaid; HCAHPS at 4.3/5.

Supply chain 31% ($57 million): GPO with HealthTrust got 17% off antibodies and implants, $30 million bundled. RFID via Omnicell cut stockouts 33%, write-offs $11 million; Vizient ERP dropped supply per discharge 8.5% to $2,420.

Florida post-hurricane hubs saved 11.5%, Texas 7.5%. Tech/RCM 19% ($35 million): Epic rollout cut denials 26% to 4.3%, AI coding lifted CMI 2 points to 1.77; RCM days to 44, $26 million cash. Teladoc virtual nursing saved $14 million, outpatient up 13% to $2.05 billion; MA at 21%.

Facilities 6% ($9 million): EnergyCAP for 14% utility cuts, LEED for Texas sites.

Total OpEx down 6.8% to $4.7 billion, EPS up 11% to $1.48. Quality intact: readmits 14.7%, NPS +2.5. 2025 eyes $195 million savings, AI maintenance with Nuance, rural divestitures. Sunbelt adds 1,100 beds de-risks.

Moving to initiatives improving operating margin: Our margin hit 9.9% in Q3, up 220 basis points YoY from 7.7%, best since pre-pandemic. On pace for 10-11% full-year, stretch 12% FY2026, ahead of HCA's 12.4% TTM.

Levers: Labor (55% costs): Flex model cut agency 34% QoQ to $75 million via Epic MySchedule, float at 84%. Southeast down to 7.5% agency; HPPD to 6.0, +75 bps. AMN partnerships target 12% FY2025 cut.

Supply (19%): Vizient deal 13% off stents/gloves; clinician committees switched 68% implants to generics, $17 million save. Cost per CMI discharge to $2,210; Texas bundled on 44% MA.

RCM: R1 AI denials to 8.5%, A/R to 44 days; $42 million uplift, rev per admission +4% to $14,100. Renegos with UHC/BCBS +3.5%; ACO REACH 27% lives, $20 million bonuses.

Efficiency: ALOS 4.5 days on Cerner AI; telemed 21% visits, OR 91% via LeanTaaS. Urban Dallas 94%; rural ED focus.

Dashboard tracks KPIs; debt/EBITDA 3.1x. $145 million CapEx for RPA. $275 million EBITDA YTD, 55% savings. 140-190 bps annual gains, 8-9% EPS.

On value-based care contracts' reimbursement impact: VBC now 29% of revenue, up from 23% YoY, 19% Q3 2023. Above HCA/CHS 21-24%.

FFS limits to DRG $6,500-12,000; VBC ties to TCOC/quality. ACOs (56% VBC): Apex ACO 118,000 lives, 95% quality, $40 million savings 9M, full $58 million; 11.5% uplift, readmits down 14%, SNF 17%.

Bundles (29%): BPCI ortho $27,500 target, 91% recon, $17 million; LOS 2.2 days. Commercial FL bundles 21% margins.

Cap/full-risk (15%): Humana MA 24,000 lives, $940 PMPM, MLR 81%. 340B/biosimilars cut drugs 9%.

Southeast (FL/GA/NC, 61% beds) 36% VBC, +$2.40/discharge; Midwest 19%, telehealth RAF +4.5 points, $9 million.

Epic QPP integration, Cerner AI cuts admits 20%; Innovaccer TCOC aims $95 million save 2025. Rev/discharge +4% to $14,100, CMI 1.84. VBC to 36% YE, +$145-195 million EBITDA. Hedged FFS carve-outs.

Operating margin specifics: 12.6% Q3, +80 bps QoQ from 11.8%, +240 bps YoY from 10.2%. Revenue +8.5% to $4.75 billion on 5.3% admits to 141,000, CMI +2.4% to 1.79; outpatient 59% mix +11.7%, 5 new ASCs Phoenix/DFW.

Expenses +7% : Labor 52%, +7.5% but agency -40% QoQ; supply +8.8% offset HealthTrust 6% pricing. QoQ: AI Waystar denials -14%, +$115 million cash, LOS 4.5, +30 bps.

Sunbelt (FL/TX/NC 63% EBITDA) 14.9%, +320 bps on MA 33%, commercial 47%; FL +7.5% admits. Northeast 9.3%, flat on unions/Medicaid; $48 million CapEx da Vinci.

Guide 12.1-12.6% FY; outpatient 66% 2025, VBC 26%, Epic virtual.

Inpatient vs. outpatient trends: Inpatient admits 141,000, -4% YoY (6,000 less), 12th quarter down, patient days 775,000 -3.5%, ALOS 5.4 stable, CMI +2.2% to 1.79 ortho/cardio.

Outpatient 2.45 million visits +8.8% YoY (190,000 more), ASC +12.7% to 176,000, HOPD +7.5% to 1.89 million; endoscopy/pain +14%/10%. Rev/encounter $1,430 +5.3%; inpatient flat $14,200.

QoQ inpatient -1.5%, outpatient +3.5%. AHA: inpatient -3%, outpatient +8%.

Drivers: MA 39% steers to ASC/UC; obs +8.5% to 21%; deductibles push same-day.

Sunbelt inpatient -1.8%, outpatient +11.5% on USPI JVs; Rust Belt -7%, outpatient +6.5%, tele 19%.

$240 million Outpatient First: 11 ASCs, Epic AI routes 64%; da Vinci 92% same-day. Oak Street funnels 14,000 visits. Margins +110 bps to 28.5%, ASC $2,750/case. CDI +$42 million; bundles readmits -17%. FY2025 inpatient flat/-1.5%, outpatient 8-11%, +$1.15 billion rev.

Payer revenue mix: Medicare 48.5% +130 bps YoY, flat QoQ; Medicaid 22% +160 bps YoY +90 bps QoQ; Commercial 24.2% -210 bps YoY -60 bps QoQ; Self-pay/other 5.3% -80 bps YoY.

Blended CMI 1.93 +2.1%; rev +6% to $2.48 billion, gov 70%.

Medicare up on boomers, surgical +7.5%, but IPPS 2.6% net. Medicaid expansion states stable, managed 103% cost. Commercial ASP -1.2% denials 11.5%; self-pay SW 9% uninsured, screening cuts bad debt 2%.

ACO REACH $27 million, MA Medicare 33%; Epic scrubbing denials -17%. Sunbelt Medicare +8.5%; Midwest commercial 31%.

Q4 steady, negotiate 106% commercial; long commercial tilt, financing. EBITDA 12.5% > peers.

Finally, same-facility guidance: Q4 rev 4.6-5.6% YoY, vol 2.6-3.6%; admits +2-3%, outpt +3.3-4.3%, rev/adm +1.9-2.4%, CMI 1.83.

FY2025 rev 4.9-6.1%, vol 3.1-4.1%; inpatient +2.6-3.6%, outpt +3.9-4.9%, rev/adm +1.8-2.5%.

Post-COVID electives 99% 2019; ER +4.2%; MA 29%. Cerner RCM A/R 44; tele +26%, Google AI beds +7%.

Sunbelt 4.3-5.3%, migration; Midwest/NE 2.1-3.1%, payer deals. ASC REIT spin; risks IPPS/staffing, retention 93%.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Lisa Patel for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Lisa Patel:
Thank you, David. Good morning. We are making significant strides in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our Integrated Care Pathways program has shown remarkable results, with an 18% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform, remote patient monitoring programs, and AI-powered diagnostic tools.

Following that, Karen Lopez will provide an update on operational efficiency.

Karen Lopez:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including lean management programs and digital workflow enhancements, which have resulted in significant cost savings, improved patient flow, and enhanced staff productivity.

Next, Tom Ellis will discuss our strategic initiatives.

Tom Ellis:
Thank you, Karen. Our strategic priorities remain focused on expanding our network, developing new partnerships, and investing in innovative technologies. We are actively exploring opportunities to grow our footprint in key markets, enhance our service offerings, and diversify our revenue streams.

After that, Raj Singh will discuss our IT infrastructure and cybersecurity.

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Tom. We are committed to maintaining a robust and secure IT infrastructure to support our operations and protect patient data. We have implemented several new security measures to enhance our cybersecurity posture, ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, and mitigate the risk of data breaches. We are also investing in cloud-based solutions to improve scalability and flexibility.

Following that, Emily Grant will discuss our efforts related to workforce development and employee engagement.

Emily Grant:
Thank you, Raj. We are committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly skilled and engaged workforce. We are implementing several initiatives to improve employee satisfaction, enhance training and development opportunities, and promote a culture of diversity and inclusion.

Finally, Mark Reynolds will elaborate on our compliance efforts.

Mark Reynolds:
Thank you, Emily. We are dedicated to maintaining the highest standards of ethical conduct and regulatory compliance. We have implemented a comprehensive compliance program to ensure adherence to all applicable laws and regulations, protect patient privacy, and prevent fraud and abuse.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Mike Rivera.

Mike Rivera:
Thank you, everyone. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for participating in the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more details on the specific initiatives you are implementing to improve employee satisfaction and retention?

Emily Grant:
Good morning, John. Absolutely. We're prioritizing a holistic approach to workforce well-being, building on our labor optimization successes. Key efforts include dynamic staffing with AI predictive scheduling to reduce burnout by balancing workloads, achieving 92% forecast accuracy and cutting overtime 24%. We've rolled out premium incentives linked to retention KPIs, boosting hours per patient day efficiency while holding HCAHPS steady. Training via digital platforms enhances skills in high-demand areas like sepsis pathways, and our diversity programs have lifted engagement scores 12%. In Sunbelt markets, we've seen retention rise to 94% with localized flex pools. These are complemented by mental health resources and career development paths, targeting 95% retention by year-end.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
What are your plans for addressing the ongoing challenges related to regulatory compliance and cybersecurity threats?

Mark Reynolds:
Thanks, Lisa. Compliance and cyber are foundational. Our program includes real-time Epic-QPP integration for MIPS, quarterly payer audits keeping clawbacks under 1.5%, and 340B optimization. For cyber, new multi-factor layers and annual penetration tests exceed HIPAA, with cloud migrations via AWS enhancing breach response to under 24 hours. We've trained 98% staff via phishing sims, and partnerships like Innovaccer dashboards monitor risks. Amid No Surprises Act, arbitration success is 85%. We're ahead on site-neutral prep, targeting zero material fines.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel:
Can you elaborate on the potential impact of your strategic acquisitions on your long-term growth prospects?

Tom Ellis:
Hi Mike. Our recent acquisitions, like two Sunbelt ASC clusters adding 1,000 procedures annualized, accelerate ambulatory shift, projecting 10% revenue CAGR through 2027. They boost MA penetration to 30% in key MSAs, with bundled ortho margins at 25%. Synergies from Epic integration yield $20 million savings Year 1, de-risking inpatient softness. Long-term, they support 15% EBITDA growth, mirroring Tenet/USPI, with $500 million tuck-ins planned for high-growth TX/FL.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Anna Rodriguez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Anna Rodriguez:
How are you leveraging AI to improve diagnostic accuracy?

Dr. Lisa Patel:
Great question, Anna. Our AI diagnostics, via Cerner Revenue Cycle Insights and homegrown models on 5-year claims, flag high-risk cases like CHF pre-admission, cutting avoidable admits 21% and boosting CMI capture. In pathways, predictive discharge flags 86% cases early, LOS down 0.3 days. Telehealth AI triage diverts 33% low-acuity, preserving beds. Pilots with Nuance Dragon yield 95% quality on eCQMs, enhancing VBC bonuses $25 million. Accuracy rivals peers, with 14.5% readmits vs. national 16.5%.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes the question-and-answer session.

Mike Rivera:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Apex Health Systems Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
